page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.xlarge is an arm64-based server instance powered by the custom Alibaba Yitian 710 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.75 GHz with 1 thread per core, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, positioning it as a memory-optimized instance. The server operates on the KVM hypervisor, includes a 64 MB L3 cache, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several standard workloads, alongside notable hardware-specific limitations. The instance achieves average results in stress-ng single-core (1819.58) and multi-core (7234.41) tests, as well as average Redis SET operations at 6.4 million operations per second. However, the arm64 architecture lacks AVX, AMX, and BMI2 instruction sets, contributing to weak PassMark CPU scores (3466.43) and poor CPU encryption test results (654.15). Memory read bandwidth is average at 409.68 GB/sec for small cached blocks, but large block write bandwidth is weak at 24.45 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the custom ARM-based architecture offers high memory density per vCPU, allowing memory-intensive applications to run without the overhead of paying for unneeded compute cores. Tradeoffs include weak static web serving throughput (6.29 GB/sec) and poor text generation speeds for larger models, such as 4.59 tokens per second on a 7B LLM. This instance is best suited for memory-bound workloads that do not rely heavily on x86-specific vector instructions, such as caching layers, Redis databases, and moderate database operations.
